personal_visual_observations.observation: Proximal fibula is visible at the right side of the displayed image, adjacent to the tibia. Its lateral anatomical position is consistent across the two independently acquired coronal sequences. Each image contains one knee.

Proximal fibula is visible at the left side of the displayed image, opposite the left-tag group. Each image contains one knee. Sagittal and transverse sample panels also show separately acquired single-knee anatomy but the coronal fibular landmark is the direct side discriminator used.

orientation_reasoning.rendering: Renderer displays native 2D stored arrays through imshow with no transpose, flip, or anatomical reorientation. Percentile contrast affects intensity only. Increasing image column therefore moves right in the displayed panel.
orientation_reasoning.reason: For a biped patient, DICOM +x is patient left; the first IOP triplet is direction along increasing column. Both coronal groups have first-direction x near+1. Thus fibula at display right is lateral toward patient left, consistent with the left knee; fibula at display left is lateral toward patient right, consistent with the right knee. Obliquity is small and does not reverse the left-right direction. This conclusion depends on correct IOP and absence of unrecorded pixel mirroring upstream.

conclusion.confidence_description: Strong technical evidence from a consistent lateral anatomical landmark plus recorded orientation, corroborated by explicit two-sided source text and two repeated acquisition groups. Not based on missing laterality alone.
